sources.label: WICG — WebRTC Diagnostic Logging API (incubation document)
Chrome Platform Showcase — WebRTC Diagnostic Logging API

inputs.rationale: The operation takes no arguments - the IDL declares an empty parameter list - so there is no input contract, default or validation rule to state. This is an absence of the dimension, not unstated content.
The operation takes no arguments - the IDL declares an empty parameter list - so there is no input contract to document; the discard behaviour is an effect of the call, not a parameter.
A dictionary has no constructor and no call of its own; it is never invoked, only populated as the options argument of startDiagnosticLogging, which is where its input contract is stated.

errors.rationale: The dictionary itself throws nothing: the metadata limits that can fail are validated by startDiagnosticLogging's steps and are documented on that method and on the metadata member, not here.

lifecycle.rationale: A dictionary is a value passed into a call; it has no creation, teardown or state of its own. The session lifecycle it feeds is documented on the three methods.

The member is a plain record of strings carried by the session; the specification gives it no created, consumed or discarded state of its own. Its limits are checked when the session starts, which is documented on the startDiagnosticLogging row.

notes: THIS CONTRACT COULD NOT BE WRITTEN AGAINST THE PAGE AS IT STOOD, and that is why the page was migrated first: until 2026-07-27 the cited document described navigator.rtc with an RTC interface, a finishDiagnosticLogging method, promise returns and an allowUpload option, and the page mirrored it. The source was rewritten that day to static methods on RTCPeerConnection, so the page's syntax no longer matched the document it cited - and because the schema requires syntax, examples and compatibility to be documented, a contract written before the rewrite could only have certified a superseded draft against a citation that contradicted it. The migration and this contract therefore land together, in one change. FIVE ROWS, and the accounting is exact: the page's declared surface is four members (startDiagnosticLogging, stopDiagnosticLogging, cancelDiagnosticLogging, metadata) and all four are inventoried, so outOfScope is empty rather than padded; the fifth row is RTCDiagnosticLoggingOptions, which is not a declared member but is a real documented item - the dictionary has its own syntax, its own context and its own single member - so folding it into the method rows would have been the fragment-inheritance defect in reverse. AUTHORITATIVE-SURFACE POLICY, and it is deliberate rather than tidy: ALL THREE documents in the chain still hurt themselves, and the page records each mismatch instead of silently resolving it. THE WICG INCUBATION DOCUMENT is the one that holds the stale wording: its section heading for the third operation reads discardDiagnosticLogging while its IDL declares cancelDiagnosticLogging, and its startDiagnosticLogging metadata step still says 'return a promise rejected with a TypeError' although the operation is now synchronous. THE W3C SPECIFICATION, which this page cites as canonical, has neither of THOSE two problems - it says cancelDiagnosticLogging throughout and already states that the startDiagnosticLogging metadata step throws a TypeError - and the attribution matters: a note that blamed 'the specification' would be false about the document the page actually cites. The third mismatch is in the explainer, whose example still calls the second operation finishDiagnosticLogging and the third cancelLogging. A FOURTH recorded mismatch is inside that same canonical document, and it is the one that does not fit the 'authoritative surface' reading of the chain: THE W3C SPECIFICATION IS INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT ABOUT WHERE THE SESSION SLOT LIVES. Its Internal slots section defines [[RTCDiagnosticLoggingSessionId]] on the relevant global object, while its algorithm steps reference RTCPeerConnection/[[RTCDiagnosticLoggingSessionId]]. This is a defect in the document the page cites as canonical rather than in the incubation copy, so it is attributed here to the W3C document by name and NOT counted among the incubation document's stale-wordings above. The page follows the Internal slots definition and records the discrepancy on startDiagnosticLogging, because silently choosing between two definitions inside one document would leave the next reader unable to tell which half was followed. The IDL governs the identifiers implementers type, so the page documents cancelDiagnosticLogging and stopDiagnosticLogging - but it says out loud where the names disagree, because a silent correction would make the next reader who searches the source for 'discard' conclude the page invented a name. The three InvalidStateError throws are stated per method and each traces to its own normative steps: start throws when the session slot is NOT null, stop and cancel throw when it IS null. The WICG incubation document mentions the exception seven times but throws it three; the other four are its term index and cross-reference data, which is why the count is taken from the algorithms rather than from a text search. INPUTS IS NOT-APPLICABLE ON stop, cancel AND THE DICTIONARY, but documented on start and on metadata, and the distinction is the whole point rather than an inconsistency: a method with an empty parameter list and a dictionary that is only ever passed as a value have no input contract, whereas metadata IS the input - the caller supplies it, with a stated type and hard limits - so marking it not-applicable would have hidden the one place the page tells an implementer what they may pass. TWO ACCURACY CORRECTIONS RODE WITH THE MIGRATION. The page called RTCDiagnosticLogging 'status: experimental'; it is now status {Android: '', default: 'stable'} in runtime_enabled_features.json5, while the PRE-REWRITE surface moved to a separate RTCLegacyDiagnosticLogging entry that is still experimental - so the page had been naming the wrong flag for the wrong surface, and the --enable-blink-features line pointed at the new surface while the prose called it experimental. And the origin-trial window was 150-155; ChromeStatus now records 151-156 on desktop only, with ship estimate 156 and origin_trial_id 352969620795162625. The feature has also moved standards home: the canonical link is now the W3C WebRTC Extensions Diagnostic Logging section at Working draft, so the page cites that document as primary and keeps the WICG document as the incubation copy serving the same surface. THE EMBEDDED DEMO IS DECLARED STALE ON THE PAGE: all four showcase routes still call the pre-rewrite surface - measured 2026-10-06, they contain navigator.rtc, three of the four also contain allowUpload, and ZERO occurrences of stopDiagnosticLogging or RTCPeerConnection - so the page states that plainly, with the reading date and the reason (those demos live in the Chrome Platform Showcase repository, not this one), and points the reader at the snippet instead. A page that silently changed only the half it owns would be wrong about its source, its example and its own coherence at once. The BCD absence is asserted on the strength of a controlled probe, not a guess: api/RTCPeerConnection.json holds 52 top-level keys, 51 of them members, the positive controls close, createOffer, connectionState and setConfiguration are all present, and no diagnostic or logging member exists - the first probe I ran was discarded precisely because it also reported close.json absent, which is what a control is for. Finally, this page's conformance.json is untouched: its identity and suiteHash are unchanged and none of its assertions name the old surface, which was verified BEFORE any editing because a changed conformance suite would have removed the touched-page exemption and made this unit's scope larger than it is.
